bibl.title: Slingshot: cell lineage and pseudotime inference for single-cell transcriptomics

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the inference of branching cell lineages and pseudotime from single-cell transcriptomics - that is, RECOVERING A DEVELOPMENTAL ORDER THAT WAS NEVER OBSERVED, from cells all captured at once
span.quote: For many systems, there are not clear distinctions between cellular states, but instead a smooth transition, where individual cells represent points along a continuum or lineage . Cells in these systems change states by undergoing gradual transcriptional changes, with progress being driven by an underlying temporal variable or pseudotime

span.label: how to identify multiple branching lineages, and their pseudotimes, stably enough to survive the noise of single-cell data and without requiring the number of lineages in advance
span.quote: Slingshot allows for multiple lineage detection without pre-specifying or limiting the number of lineages. Instead, Slingshot provides a framework for optional incorporation of localized prior biological knowledge that does not restrict other parts of the tree or introduce global specifications.

span.label: Slingshot - a cluster-based minimum spanning tree for the global structure, then SIMULTANEOUS PRINCIPAL CURVES for the pseudotimes - plus a benchmark against five existing methods on real and 1,500 simulated datasets
span.quote: In its first step, Slingshot identifies lineages by treating clusters of cells as nodes in a graph and drawing a minimum spanning tree (MST) between the nodes, similar to the work of [ 7 , 10 ]. Lineages are then defined as ordered sets of clusters created by tracing paths through the MST, starting from a given root node. Our method differs however in a number of important respects from those of [ 7 , 10 ] including the distance measure used for drawing the tree and the (optional) incorporation of biologically meaningful supervision.

span.label: method
span.quote: In its first step, Slingshot identifies lineages by treating clusters of cells as nodes in a graph and drawing a minimum spanning tree (MST) between the nodes, similar to the work of [ 7 , 10 ]. Lineages are then defined as ordered sets of clusters created by tracing paths through the MST, starting from a given root node. Our method differs however in a number of important respects from those of [ 7 , 10 ] including the distance measure used for drawing the tree and the (optional) incorporation of biologically meaningful supervision.

span.label: a continuum of transcriptional states in which cells sit at points along one or more branching trajectories, with no discrete boundaries and no observed time
span.quote: For many systems, there are not clear distinctions between cellular states, but instead a smooth transition, where individual cells represent points along a continuum or lineage . Cells in these systems change states by undergoing gradual transcriptional changes, with progress being driven by an underlying temporal variable or pseudotime

span.label: an MST drawn over CELL CLUSTERS rather than cells, treating clusters as graph nodes, with lineages read off as the paths from a root; the distance measure and an optional biologically-motivated supervision are what the paper names as its departures from the same first stage in TSCAN and Waterfall. The evaluation design and the scoring rule are tagged separately, each on its own sentence
span.term: an MST drawn over CELL CLUSTERS rather than cells, treating clusters as graph nodes, with lineages read off as the paths from a root; the distance measure and an optional biologically-motivated supervision are what the paper names as its departures from the same first stage in TSCAN and Waterfall. The evaluation design and the scoring rule are tagged separately, each on its own sentence
span.quote: In its first step, Slingshot identifies lineages by treating clusters of cells as nodes in a graph and drawing a minimum spanning tree (MST) between the nodes, similar to the work of [ 7 , 10 ]. Lineages are then defined as ordered sets of clusters created by tracing paths through the MST, starting from a given root node. Our method differs however in a number of important respects from those of [ 7 , 10 ] including the distance measure used for drawing the tree and the (optional) incorporation of biologically meaningful supervision.

span.label: the stability tracks WHAT THE TREE IS BUILT ON. Monocle builds its MST on INDIVIDUAL CELLS and `was the LEAST STABLE of the methods we compared`, with a path `highly variable and sensitive to even small amounts of noise`. Slingshot builds it on clusters. The paper reports the association; the averaging account of WHY is mine
span.quote: The Monocle procedure, which constructs an MST on individual cells and orders them according to a PQ tree along the longest path of the MST, was the least stable of the methods we compared. The path drawn by Monocle was highly variable and sensitive to even small amounts of noise; this instability has been previously discussed in

span.label: and the same separation is what makes the result robust to the CLUSTERING method while remaining sensitive to K: the curves smooth over where the cluster centres happen to fall, but they cannot invent a branch the MST did not find
span.quote: Although Slingshot uses cluster labels for the identification of lineages and branching events, the subsequent use of simultaneous principal curves to obtain pseudotimes makes its final results quite robust to the choice of clustering method.

span.label: EVERY METHOD IN THIS FIELD, INCLUDING THIS ONE, REQUIRES PART OF THE ANSWER AS INPUT: `all existing lineage inference methods explicitly or implicitly make the assumption that A STARTING STATE CAN BE IDENTIFIED BY THE USER`. Slingshot asks for the initial cluster; Wishbone and DPT for an initial cell; Monocle and Embeddr for the direction of a path. THE ARROW OF DEVELOPMENT IS NOT IN THE DATA
span.quote: Indeed, all existing lineage inference methods explicitly or implicitly make the assumption that a starting state can be identified by the user: Monocle and Embeddr construct orderings for which the user must select the correct direction and Wishbone and DPT require the user to select an initial cell or group of cells.

span.label: the upstream choices - normalisation, dimensionality reduction, clustering - have `a potentially large impact on the final result`, and the paper does not fix them. That is a deliberate design decision (`these choices should therefore NOT BE HARDCODED`) and it means A SLINGSHOT RESULT IS NOT REPRODUCIBLE FROM THE METHOD NAME ALONE
span.quote: In addition to Slingshot’s core methodological components described above for lineage and pseudotime inference, we note the importance of upstream analysis choices. Indeed, most pseudotemporal reconstruction methods will either explicitly or implicitly require certain choices at previous steps in the workflow. Dimensionality reduction, for example, helps in reducing the amount of noise in the data and in visualization, but a variety of approaches are available, with a potentially large impact on the final result

span.label: K, THE NUMBER OF CLUSTERS, IS THE PARAMETER THAT MATTERS, AND IT FAILS AT BOTH ENDS: at K=3 `Slingshot is often unable to detect the branching event`, and at higher K it `begins to OVERFIT and identify more spurious branching events`. The paper reports both, which is more than the robustness-to-clustering result on its own would suggest
span.quote: However, when K =3, Slingshot is often unable to detect the branching event and the resulting pseudotimes imperfectly match either true lineage. With more clusters, we see consistently accurate results. At higher values of K (not shown), accuracy scores begin to degrade slowly, as Slingshot begins to overfit and identify more spurious branching events.

span.label: and it says the failure is not its own: `these issues are COMMON TO ALL CLUSTER-BASED MST METHODS and NOT MITIGATED by the use of simultaneous principal curves` - the smoothing helps the pseudotimes, not the topology
span.quote: In extreme cases with too few clusters, the cluster-based MST may fail to identify a branching event, and with too many, it may identify spurious branching events. These issues are common to all cluster-based MST methods and not mitigated by the use of simultaneous principal curves.

span.label: the output is A POINT ESTIMATE WITH NO INTERVAL. The paper names two distinct uncertainties it does not quantify - STRUCTURAL (which lineage a cell belongs to) and TEMPORAL (where along it) - and offers a bootstrap as something a user could do, not as something the method does
span.quote: For branching lineage structures, there are two inextricably linked sources of uncertainty: the assignment of cells to lineages (“structural uncertainty”) and the calculation of each cell’s pseudotime (“temporal uncertainty”). While Slingshot only provides point estimates of lineage identities and pseudotimes, we note that it is generally computationally fast enough to be used in a bootstrap estimation procedure.

span.label: the real-data demonstration was SUPERVISED WITH THE ANSWER IT IS JUDGED AGAINST: the HBC cluster was given as the origin and mSus as a terminal state, and correctness is then agreement with known biology. The paper is careful enough to report which supervision mattered - `ONLY THE FIRST HAD AN EFFECT on the eventual cluster-based MST` - which is what keeps this a caveat rather than a circularity
span.quote: This local supervision was used in the analysis of the olfactory epithelium (OE) data of [ 26 ] to mark mature sustentacular (mSus) cells, microvillous (MV) cells, and mature olfactory sensory neurons (mOSN) as terminal states, though only the first had an effect on the eventual cluster-based MST.

span.label: the clustering METHOD was varied - hierarchical, k-means and Gaussian mixture modelling - across a range of K, on the two-lineage simulations
span.note: eliminates: the choice of clustering algorithm as an explanation of Slingshot's accuracy; the distributions are similar across all three · outcome: held
span.quote: For the three methods examined (hierarchical clustering, k -means, and Gaussian mixture modeling), Slingshot consistently produced similar distributions of accuracy scores over a range of values for K

span.label: K, the NUMBER of clusters, was varied over the same simulations
span.note: eliminates: nothing - and the paper says so at both ends: at K=3 the branching event is often missed, and at high K spurious branches appear. THE ONE UPSTREAM CHOICE THAT SURVIVES AS A REAL DEPENDENCE · outcome: failed
span.quote: However, when K =3, Slingshot is often unable to detect the branching event and the resulting pseudotimes imperfectly match either true lineage. With more clusters, we see consistently accurate results. At higher values of K (not shown), accuracy scores begin to degrade slowly, as Slingshot begins to overfit and identify more spurious branching events.

span.label: the competitor was handicapped IN ITS OWN FAVOUR and it is declared: `since it cannot detect branching, MONOCLE WAS ALWAYS GIVEN THE CORRECT NUMBER OF LINEAGES`
span.note: eliminates: the objection that Monocle's scores understate it because it cannot count lineages - it was not asked to · outcome: held
span.quote: Since it cannot detect branching, Monocle was always given the correct number of lineages.

span.label: whether the simulator's own shape favours the proposed method
span.note: eliminates: nothing, and the direction is AGAINST the authors: splatter's bifurcations are `sharp rather than curved`, `WHICH MAY DISADVANTAGE METHODS THAT ASSUME SMOOTHNESS, SUCH AS SLINGSHOT AND DPT`. A declared bias against one's own result is the rarest thing in this corpus · outcome: partial
span.quote: Finally, we note that the bifurcation events present in datasets generated by splatter are “sharp” rather than curved (see Additional file 1 : Figure S7), which may disadvantage methods that assume smoothness, such as Slingshot and DPT.

span.label: whether the best-of-strategies protocol is fair to a method that chooses its own parameters
span.note: eliminates: nothing, and the paper names the problem itself: TSCAN `has BUILT-IN METHODS for selecting both J' and K. THIS USER-FRIENDLINESS UNFORTUNATELY MEANS THAT THERE ARE FEWER PARAMETERS OVER WHICH WE COULD TRY DIFFERENT STRATEGIES`. THE BENCHMARK'S UNIT IS A METHOD PLUS A SET OF CHOICES, so automating the choices costs you strategies to be best over · outcome: failed
span.quote: We also note that our comparison may be slightly unfavorable for TSCAN, because it has built-in methods for selecting both J ′ (the reduced number of dimensions) and K (the number of clusters). This user-friendliness unfortunately means that there are fewer parameters over which we could try different strategies, hence our implementations without full-quantile normalization and as part of a hybrid method with Slingshot.

span.label: pseudotime
span.quote: For each lineage, identification of pseudotimes , i.e., a one-dimensional variable representing each cell’s transcriptional progression toward the terminal state. This is achieved by a method which extends principal curves

span.label: lineage
span.quote: Identification of lineages , i.e., ordered sets of cell clusters, where all lineages share a starting cluster and each leads to a unique terminal cluster. This is achieved by constructing an MST on clusters of cells.

span.label: Slingshot
span.quote: Slingshot consists of two main stages: 1) the inference of the global lineage structure and 2) the inference of pseudotime variables for cells along each lineage (Fig. 1 ). Like other methods [ 7 , 10 ], Slingshot’s first stage uses a cluster-based MST to stably identify the key elements of the global lineage structure, i.e., the number of lineages and where they branch (Fig. 1 , Step 1 ). This allows us to identify novel lineages while also accommodating the use of domain-specific knowledge to supervise parts of the tree (e.g., terminal cellular states). For the second stage, we propose a novel method called simultaneous principal curves , to fit smooth branching curves to these lineages, thereby translating the knowledge of global lineage structure into stable estimates of the underlying cell-level pseudotime variable for each lineage

span.label: cluster-based MST
span.quote: Slingshot consists of two main stages: 1) the inference of the global lineage structure and 2) the inference of pseudotime variables for cells along each lineage (Fig. 1 ). span.label: cluster-based MST methods
span.quote: In extreme cases with too few clusters, the cluster-based MST may fail to identify a branching event, and with too many, it may identify spurious branching events. These issues are common to all cluster-based MST methods and not mitigated by the use of simultaneous principal curves.

span.label: Kendall rank correlation coefficient
span.quote: The accuracy of inferred pseudotimes was measured as follows: for each true lineage, identify the best match amongst all inferred lineages, according to the Kendall rank correlation coefficient between the true and inferred pseudotime variables. Averaging these values over all true lineages yields the accuracy score for a particular method on a particular dataset.

span.label: accuracy score
span.quote: The accuracy of inferred pseudotimes was measured as follows: for each true lineage, identify the best match amongst all inferred lineages, according to the Kendall rank correlation coefficient between the true and inferred pseudotime variables. Averaging these values over all true lineages yields the accuracy score for a particular method on a particular dataset.

span.label: supervision
span.quote: Slingshot allows two forms of supervision during lineage identification: initial state and terminal states specification. Like other methods (TSCAN, Waterfall, Monocle 2), Slingshot requires the user to identify the initial cluster or root node. Subsequently, every direct path from this node to a leaf node (i.e., a cluster with only one edge) will be called a lineage.

span.label: simultaneous principal curves
span.quote: Although Slingshot uses cluster labels for the identification of lineages and branching events, the subsequent use of simultaneous principal curves to obtain pseudotimes makes its final results quite robust to the choice of clustering method.

span.label: structural uncertainty
span.quote: For branching lineage structures, there are two inextricably linked sources of uncertainty: the assignment of cells to lineages (“structural uncertainty”) and the calculation of each cell’s pseudotime (“temporal uncertainty”). While Slingshot only provides point estimates of lineage identities and pseudotimes, we note that it is generally computationally fast enough to be used in a bootstrap estimation procedure.

span.label: lineage - NOT A LINEAGE OF CELLS BUT AN ORDERED SET OF CLUSTERS, `where all lineages share a starting cluster and each leads to a unique terminal cluster`. The biological object and the computational object have one name, and the second is what is computed
span.quote: Identification of lineages , i.e., ordered sets of cell clusters, where all lineages share a starting cluster and each leads to a unique terminal cluster. This is achieved by constructing an MST on clusters of cells.

span.label: pseudotime - `a ONE-DIMENSIONAL VARIABLE representing each cell's transcriptional progression toward the terminal state`. It is a coordinate along a fitted curve, not an estimate of elapsed time, and a cell in two lineages gets TWO of them
span.quote: For each lineage, identification of pseudotimes , i.e., a one-dimensional variable representing each cell’s transcriptional progression toward the terminal state. This is achieved by a method which extends principal curves

span.label: accuracy - AS OPERATIONALISED HERE, for each TRUE lineage take the BEST MATCH among the inferred ones by Kendall rank correlation, then average over true lineages. A method that returns spurious extra lineages is not penalised for them by this score unless they displace a better match
span.quote: The accuracy of inferred pseudotimes was measured as follows: for each true lineage, identify the best match amongst all inferred lineages, according to the Kendall rank correlation coefficient between the true and inferred pseudotime variables. Averaging these values over all true lineages yields the accuracy score for a particular method on a particular dataset.

span.label: supervision - HERE IT MEANS SUPPLYING THE ROOT, and the paper's claim is not that it avoids supervision but that its supervision is LOCAL: naming a terminal cluster constrains one edge and `does not restrict the discovery of novel terminal states`

span.label: the value of K at which Slingshot is often unable to detect the branching event
span.quote: However, when K =3, Slingshot is often unable to detect the branching event and the resulting pseudotimes imperfectly match either true lineage. With more clusters, we see consistently accurate results. At higher values of K (not shown), accuracy scores begin to degrade slowly, as Slingshot begins to overfit and identify more spurious branching events.

span.label: Kendall rank correlation coefficient
span.quote: The accuracy of inferred pseudotimes was measured as follows: for each true lineage, identify the best match amongst all inferred lineages, according to the Kendall rank correlation coefficient between the true and inferred pseudotime variables. Averaging these values over all true lineages yields the accuracy score for a particular method on a particular dataset.

span.label: minimum spanning tree
span.quote: In its first step, Slingshot identifies lineages by treating clusters of cells as nodes in a graph and drawing a minimum spanning tree (MST) between the nodes, similar to the work of [ 7 , 10 ]. Lineages are then defined as ordered sets of clusters created by tracing paths through the MST, starting from a given root node. Our method differs however in a number of important respects from those of [ 7 , 10 ] including the distance measure used for drawing the tree and the (optional) incorporation of biologically meaningful supervision.
